title: Contrasting repeat-divergence profiles
legend: Representation of low-divergence repeats differs across sampled reproductive strategies, with the clearest separation among LTRs. (a) LTR, LINE and TIR profiles show all 34 species as thin gray curves and equal-weight means for 7 aquatic-egg species, 24 terrestrial-egg species with aquatic larvae, and 3 direct developers as coloured curves. Each 1-percentage-point bin is expressed as its share of all RepeatMasker-aligned hit bp for that species; missing order/bin combinations are zero-filled across bins 0–49. All orders share 0–50% divergence and 0–3% aligned-hit-bp axes. No within-order normalization is applied. (b) For every species, the same all-hit denominator is used for the sum of bins 0–4, shown on matched 0–6% axes in the shared phylogenetic order. RepeatMasker alignments come from dnaPipeTE repeat-contig assemblies. Strategy comparisons are descriptive and not phylogenetically corrected. Sequence divergence is not insertion age or a measured transposition rate; aligned-hit fractions are not whole-genome occupancy. No biological confidence intervals are inferred from the aligned hits.
alt_text: Three equal-scale divergence panels show individual species and reproductive-strategy means. Below, a 34-species dot plot compares LTR, LINE and TIR fractions below 5% divergence. The three direct developers have the lowest low-divergence LTR fractions; aquatic-egg species are intermediate; terrestrial-egg species with aquatic larvae are higher.
